The weather pattern across the Marianas is influenced by a very 
broad trough and embedded weak low to the west, the remnants of 
Invest 90W to the east-southeast, and a developing monsoon pattern 
across western Micronesia. Scatterometry from this morning shows an 
area of light to gentle south-southwest to south winds across the 
coastal waters. Winds remain light to gentle tonight as they 
gradually shift southeasterly, increasing slightly tomorrow, which 
will push more of the island-effect showers off-shore in the 
afternoon. Models then depict a complex pattern unfolding over the 
next few days as the monsoon pattern strengthens south of the 
islands, and a trough looks to approach from the northeast. These 
features will interact to generate scattered showers around Tuesday 
night and Wednesday, as the overall monsoon pattern begins to lift 
northwest. Within the eastern periphery of this monsoon pattern, 
model guidance depicts the formation of a broad disturbance south to 
southwest of the Marianas in the latter half of the week. As this 
feature moves northwest and passes near or southwest of the area, at 
least scattered showers are expected, continuing into the weekend. 
There is a large degree of uncertainty in how the pattern will evolve
in the coming days. If this feature develops or passes closer to the
islands, showers may become numerous to widespread at times, and 
winds could become breezy and gusty. For now, models depict the 
disturbance developing farther west of the Marianas, keeping the 
islands along its eastern periphery.

Marine/Surf...
Light to gentle south to southeast winds will prevail across the 
Marianas through this week, becoming light to moderate Thursday. 
Combined seas of 3 to 4 feet will persist for much of the upcoming
week, increasing by a foot or so in the latter half of the week 
with an increase in southwest monsoon swell. The developing monsoon 
pattern to the south will bring increasing chances for showers and 
thunderstorms toward the end of the week. Meanwhile, a low risk of 
rip currents is expected to continue along all reefs for the next few
days. By the end of the week, the rip risk may increase once again 
to moderate due to the increase in southwest swell.

Tropical Systems...
A tropical disturbance, Invest 90W, located north-northeast of Chuuk
near 12N153E, continued to weaken over the course of the day and 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) closed the Invest earlier this 
afternoon. Remnants of 90W will continue to blend in with the 
overarching monsoon pattern across western Micronesia.

Eastern Micronesia...
A buffer circulation south of the equator has absorbed all of the
energy from what use to be Invest 90W, with that circulation having
lost all of its deeper (stronger) convection. As a result, the mid
shift's trend of reduced rainfall potential looks good, and this was
continued through the forecast, with no mention of heavy rainfall.
Showers will still become scattered in coverage from time to time,
but the synoptic pattern is changing, with what looks like a monsoon
gyre setup developing northwest of the region. This could still send
some scattered showers towards Pohnpei, but for now just showers in
the southwest to westerly flow looks to be the main mechanism for
convective development the next few days, possibly longer.

Seas look to remain in the 4 to 6 foot range, slightly lower east of
the atolls as they disrupt wave fetch length. Mainly light to gentle
winds will persist well into next week.

Western Micronesia...
Invest 90W has shifted north of Chuuk State and has weakened. For
this reason, JTWC has closed this Invest. Periods of locally heavy 
showers will continue to be associated with a monsoon pattern across 
western Micronesia over the next few days. An area of diffluence 
between the remnants of 90W and a broad circulation south of the 
equator is fragmenting the leading edge of the monsoon pattern over 
Chuuk State this evening. Still, light to moderate westerly winds and
scattered to numerous showers continue through midweek due to the 
proximity of the monsoon trough. The last Special Weather Statement 
was issued this evening to conclude related impacts with 90W.

For Yap and Palau, a Special Weather Statement was issued for the 
developing monsoon pattern in the region. This pattern is producing 
fresh west-southwesterlies and a surge of numerous to widespread 
locally heavy showers and thunderstorms, accompanied by strong to 
near-gale gusts. There is some indication that a broad monsoon 
disturbance will gradually form to the north-northeast, which could 
lead to an intensified monsoon surge across Palau and Yap. Model 
trends indicate 3 to 5 inches of rainfall through midweek. There is
